FOREWORD

0.1 This Indian Standard was adopted by the Indian Standards Institution all 17 November 1968, after the draft finalized by the Wood Products Sectional Committee had been approved by the Civil Engineering Division
0.2 Medium strength aircraft plywood suitable for use mainly in secondary structural parts of aircrafts and gliders has been covered in IS: 709-1957*. However, for use in primary structural parts of aircraft, high-strength plywood is needed. This-standard has, therefore, been formulated to lay down the requirements of high strength plywood for use in primary structural parts of aircraft: 0.3 In the formulation this standard due weightage has been gigen to international co-ordinatjon among the standards and practices prevaiOng in different countries in aadition to relating it to the practices in the ftld in this country. '
'f

or

~

0.4 This standard contains clause 3.2.2 which permits the purchasea to specify the type of adhesive required for binding of the veneers. 1 r 0.5 For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance with IS: 2-196Qt., The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard.

I. SCOPE 1.1 This standard lays down the requirements for strength, quality J bonding and manufacture of high strength aircraft plywood suitable for use in the manufacture of primary structural parts of aircraft.

2. TERMINOLOGY 2.8 For the purpose of this standard, definitions given in IS: 707.1968.
and the following shall apply. 2.1

.dl- The side of the panel opposite to the face.

2.2 Batdl- Plywood boards of the same thickness produced from the
same material and on the same day in one press from the same roll of film adhesive or mix of adhesives.

2.3 BUner - Spot or area where the veneers do not adhere together
properly and bulge like a blister.

2.4 BireI'. Eye - A small roughly circular marking due to contorted
grain.

2.5 Brash Wood-Wood which breaks with a short fracture, that is with little or no splintering due to fungal attack or other causes. 2.6 Barr-A lump
tlr

a knot

011

the base of a tree trunk.

2.7 Cheek -A separation of the fibres extending along tile grain which does not affect the entire thickness of a veneer or ply.

2.8 Core- The inner layer or layers of plywood.
2.9 Deeay - Di!iintegratiorl of wood tissues caused by wood-destroying fungi. 2.10 Delamination - Separation of adjacent plies partial or complete caused by poor or defective glue adhesion, 2.11 DiseoloaratioD - Patch of a colour differing from that normally associated with the species and occurring in either streaks or patches.

2.12 Dote -- Patch or streak of decay differing frorn surrounding wood chiefly in colour indicating incipient decay. It may be Iighter or darker
than the normal. 2.13 Eclle Jolat-- A joint made between two v.... neers in the general direction of the grain. 2.14 Eacl Jolat - A joint made between two veneers across the grain. 2.15 EsteDcler - A substance added mainly to reduce the cost of gluing. 2.16 F.ce.....-- The better side of the pane) in allY grade calling for a face and a back; also either side of a panel where the grading rules draw no distinction between faces. 2.17 FWer-An inert substance, such as wood flour, added to alter the characteristics (for example to reduce brlttleneas-) of a synthetic resin.

2.11 Gap - A void in the core due to a split or edges of adjacent veneen not being close. 2.11 Ia.ect Hole ( Borer Hole) - A hole caused by the attack of woodboring insects.

2.11.1 Harmless Inset' Hole (Borer Hole) - Insect hole with no Jiving borers, and not exceeding 1-6 rnm in diameter.
2.20 lr"lDlar Grai. - A comprehensive term, covering all cases where the grain, noticeably, is not parallel to the appropriate edges and to the face of the veneer. The main forms of irregular grain are short grain. wavy grain and wild grain.

2.20.1 Short Grain - This results from crook in the log. It is also present in more acute form surrounding or in close proximity to knots, when it is caused by the knife of the veneer cutting machine cutting across the wood with which the branch was enveloped in the growing tree; in such instances the inclination of the grain to the face of the veneer may approach 90� in the .extreme case. 2.20.2 Wavy Grain - "he fibres are wavy, hut the waviness is in the plane of the veneer. Where waviness is present it is generally fairly uniform and continuous, . 2.20.3 Wild Grain-Wild grain occurs when the log has a co.....ted exterior. When such a 109 is peeled the fibres run in and out of the suJface of the veneer in transverse bands corresponding to the ridges on th11og. The evenness of the peeling cut is disturbed, resulting in a ridged stfCace in these bands, in addition to the inclined growth. 't
~~

2!21 bot - A portion of a branch embedded in the wood by the rut'tura1
growth of the tree.
~
,

2.21.1 D,ad Knot - A knot not firmly joined throughout to the surreunding wood, sometimes including bark.

2.21.2 Decayed Knot-A knot which, due to advanced decay, it not as hard as the surrounding wood.

2.21.3 [""'grown Knot (or Tight Knot) - A knot whose rings of annual growth are completely intergrown with those of the surrounding wood. 2.21.4 LivI Knot (or Sound Knot) - A tight knot free from decay and cracks, firmly joined throughout to the surrounding wood.

2.22 Metal CUp or Staple - Fastener used in the assembly of plywood to
prevent movement of the veneers during processing. removed from the finished product. ) due to overlapping of two adjacent core veneers.

2.24 Patda - A piece of sound veneer placed in and glued to a veneer from which the defective portion has been removed.

2.25 Pleat - A defect due to a veneer being folded parallel to the grain
forming three thicknesses locally.

2.26 Ply - The individual layer of veneer forming the plywood.

2.26.1 T'hree-Pty-:� Plywood board made of three layers of veneer. 2.2&.2 Multi-PI1- Plywood board made of more than three la vers of

2.27 Plywoocl- A board fonned of three or more layers of veneer
cemented or glued together usually with the grain of adjacent veneers running at right angles to each other.

2.28 Searl Jobat - A joint made by bonding together two bevelled edges,
2.29 SpUt - A separation of the fibres along the grain in a veneer extending from face to face.

2.29.1 Closld Split-A split in which the two adjacent edges are in close contact with each other.
2.21.2 O/JIn Split- A split in which the two adjacent edges are not in
close contact with each other.

2.30 Tape--Strip of gummed paper or similar material used to hold together the edges of a joint or split during manufacture.

3.1.1 In selecting the species for manufacturing- of plywood it is recommended that as far as possible a single species of timber be used for all plies; where combination of species is used, a single species of timber should be used for both face and back plies and care should be taken to prevent incompatii-ility of species.
NOTB -- Other species of timber, such as (a) rosewood (Dalb,rgifJ lntifolJIl Roxb ), (b) auoo (Dalbergitr stssoo Roxb ), (c) walnut (juglans sp), (d) padauk (pterocarpus dalb",ioid8S Roxb ), (e) teak t Tecton� grandu Linn f), (f) mullilarn (FaRaTa budnunga Roxb), (g) sandan (Ongerrlll oojeinensis ), (h) padri (Sll',Oj!JI'mum 'p), (j) debadaru ( PtJlyaJ'hia sp ), and (k) hollock (terminalla myriocarpa Heurck et Muell. Arg) may also be used provided that l}JI... construction is established to be satisfactory in actual use and in addition the performance specified in this standard is satisfied.

"4

" the 4.1 V. .eer. - The veneers shall be. either rotary cut or sliced fro.. timber species specified under 3.1. Sap wood shall not be permit_d in veneers.

4.2 The thickness of veneers shall not exceed 3 mm,
43 The grain in veneers shall be straight and shall run parallel to the edges, except as permitted under 4.4.

4.4 The slopes of the grain from the edge of the veneer shall be not greater than I in 12 nor shall the slope of the grain from the plane of veneer be greater than 1 in 12.

4.5 The veneer shall be reasonably free from irregular grain, such as short grain, wavy grain and wild grain.

6.2 The finished sheets shall be smooth and free from blisters, overlaps, pleats, gaps and open joints. The surface shall be free from oil wax, paraffin, tape and any other substance which may prevent adhesion of glue or paint finishes. 6.3 The board shall be sanded on both faces.

7. ADHESION OF PUES
7.1 The adhesion of plies shall be tested by forcibly separating the layers. The veneers shall offer appreciable resistance to separation and the fractured samples shall show some adherent fibres distributed more or less uniformly. Adhesion may also be tested by knife test described in Appendix A of IS: 709-1957*. When tested for glue adhesion by the method described in Appendix A the average failing load shall not be less than 135 kg and no individual value shall be less than 100 kg.

a.

RESISTANCE TO WATER

11. MARKING
11.1 The following particulars shall be legibly and indelibly stamped on one side of each board:
a) b) c) d) e) f) g) Name of manufacturer or trade-mark, if any; Number of specification; Veneer species (symbol ); Thickness of board; The type of adhesives used; Date of manufacture; and Batch number and press load number.

11.1.1 Each board may also be marked with the lSI Certification Mark.
NOl'It - The use of the lSI Certification Mark is governed by the proviaious the Indian Standard. Institution ( Certification Marks) Act. and the R.ules and ~u. lations made thereunder. Presence of this mark on products covered by an Indum

Standard conveys the assurance that they have been produced to comply with the requirements of that It an dard, under a well-defined system of inspecnon, testing and quality control during production. This system, which is devised and supervised by lSI and operated by the producer, has the further safeguard that the products as actually marketed are continuously checked bv lSI for conformity to the standard. Details of conditions, under which a licence for the use of the lSI Certification Mark may be granted to manufacturers or processors, may be obtained from the Indian Standards Institution.

APPENDIX A
(Clause 7.1)
METHOD OF TEST FOR GLUE ADHESION A-I. OBJECT
A-I.l This test is intended to estimate the tenacity with which the bonding material holds the veneers together.

A-2. TEST SPECIMEN
A-2.1 At least two test specimens shall be cut from the board. The test pieces from ~~-I))Y pJ)W vood shall.. he prepared by making sa w cuts (St,
J.~ig.

3).

A-2.2 When the number of plies exceeds three, tile plywood shall be stripped of all except any three selected plies either by chiselling or by planning. The stripping shall be done so as to test any two of the adjoining glue joints, provided at least half the number of the specimens so tested inc ludes the innermost glue joint. The test ~I)C( imen shall be prepared by making' sa w-ruts as shown ill Fig. 3.

A-3. PROCEDURE
A-3.1 Each test specimen shall be gripped at two ends in the jaw; of a suitable machine, and shall be pulled apart. The pull should be as far as possible in the centre Iine of the central veneer. The graill of the centre ply shall be perpendicular to the direction of application of load. A-3..2 During the test, the load shall be applied to the test specimens as uniformly as possible, and so adjusted as to increase at a rate of approximately 270 kg/miTl.

IS 14859. 1968 A-3.3 The maximum load at the time of complete failure of each specimen shall be recorded. Record shall also be made as to failure whether in wood or in glue by visual examination of the area under shear. In case of wood failure the percentage wood failure shall also be recorded. Measurement shall be made of the width of the bonding surface and length of bonding surface under shear. A-3.4 In case of persistent wood failure of more than 50 percent due to thin veneers not more than 1'2 mm thick, the test shall be carried out by reducing tile length of shear area in between the grooves from 2-5 to 1-25 em. The shear strength of each specimen shall be calculated by multi. plying the failing load by 1-8.

REPORT

A-4.2 In case wood failure in an individual specimen is more than 50 percent, and the load at which the test specimen fails is less than the average, the value for such specimen shall be discarded for the purpose of averaging the shear strength. APPENDIX C i Clause 10.1)
DETERMINATION OF BENDING STRENGTH
C-l. TEST SPECIMENS
C-l.1 Test specimen shall be cut fro 01 each selected board in such a manner that: a) the length or the tevt piece is parallel to the grain direction of the face plies, and b) a joint shall run along the axis of the rest specimen, if there are such joints in the sheet. 0-1.2 The specimens shall be cut with the minimum slope of grail) from the edges. C-l.3 The specimens shall be oven dry at the time of test.

C-l.4 TIle specimen shall be 25 rom wide and of sufficient length, 10 that when bent over a mandrel of the specified diameter a parallel sided U is formed.

C-2. PROCEDURE
e-2.1 TIle ratio elf the diameter of the mandrel to the thickness of the plywood shall be as specified ill Table 4.

c-2.2 The specimens shall be bent at the specified radius to a parallel
sided U shape without support on the tension side. The specimen shall be bent once and bent again in the reverse directions.

cs,

EXAMlNA110N

e-3.1 The test specimen shall then be examined visually for fractures and separation of the plies. Breakage shall consist of fractures extending 3 rom or more across the width of the specimen. Tears along the fibre direction that begin at the edge and extend into the specimen along the grain sloping from the edge shall not be considered breakage. It shall be determined whether a specilnen breaks before removal tram the mandrel. Breakage of IDore than 20 percent or all the specimens tested shall be considered as the cause for rejection of the whole lot.
